transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I'm a health services manager, and what finally pushed me to come in is that I'm just really struggling to stay focused at work. I can sit down to review an EPIC quality report, or go into a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of paying attention, but... within a few minutes, my mind just drifts. I'll realize I'm rereading the same numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of whatever was just discussed. It's just getting really hard to keep on track.
Have you struggled with this difficulty staying focused for as long as you can remember, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's definitely not a new problem. I've been like this for as long as I can remember, honestly. Even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. My mother actually had to sit with me while I finished my homework because I would just... lose track of my assignments, or I'd completely forget to bring my books home from school. So, yeah, it's always been there.
Growing up, did you often feel like you had a 'motor' inside you that kept you moving, or did you frequently act before thinking through the consequences?

No, I can't say I really felt like that. I never had that feeling of being driven by a motor, and I wasn't really one to act impulsively. I wasn't the kid bouncing off the walls or getting into trouble for doing things without thinking. It was always more about... just drifting off or losing track of things, rather than being overly active.
Aside from these focus issues, would you say that you generally feel down, sad, or lack interest in things you usually enjoy for most of the day, most days?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed out sometimes with work and everything, but I don't feel depressed or sad. I still enjoy my weekends and doing things I like. It's just the focus part that's really getting in my way.
In your daily life, do you frequently find it difficult to keep your personal belongings or your workspace organized?

No, not really. I mean, my workspace at the clinic is pretty tidy, and I keep my things at home mostly where they belong. I don't really have an issue with losing my personal items or having a messy desk. It's more about my mind wandering than my things being disorganized.
When you are given a project or a multi-step task at work, do you often struggle to follow through and complete the instructions as they were given?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. Like, if someone gives me three or four follow-up steps after a committee meeting... I might get the first one done right away. I'll maybe even start drafting the second step. But then... the email or the spreadsheet or whatever the final submission is supposed to be, it just sits there unfinished. It usually stays like that until someone actually reminds me about it.
In your day-to-day life, do you often forget to keep appointments or fail to follow through on routine obligations?

No, I wouldn't say that. I keep a pretty tight schedule with my calendar, so I don't really miss appointments or forget to pay bills or anything like that. I manage to stay on top of those routine things just fine.
When you are trying to focus on a task, do you find that you are easily distracted by unrelated sights or sounds around you?

No, I don't think so. I mean, if the clinic is really loud or there's a lot of commotion right outside my door, I might notice it, but it doesn't really pull me away from what I'm doing. It's more my own thoughts that distract me, not really what's going on around me.
In your professional work, do you often make careless mistakes because you are not paying close enough attention to the details?

No, not really. I've been managing health services for a long time, so I'm pretty used to handling the details. I review reports and patient schedules and things like that every day, and I don't really make careless errors with them. I'm usually pretty accurate when it comes to the fine print.
